findings.claim: Mauna Loa in Hawaii covers an area larger than the whole island of Sicily
findings.truth: Mauna Loa covers 5,271 km2, more than half the island of Hawaii; Sicily is about 25,711 km2, so Mauna Loa is far smaller.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Mauna Loa (land area 5,271 km2; 'more than half the surface area of the island of Hawaii')

findings.claim: Paricutin in Mexico grew to 424 m within a single year (1943)
findings.truth: Paricutin reached about 365 m in its first eight months; 424 m was the final cone height when the eruption ended in 1952 after nine years.

findings.claim: The four plate boundary types are destructive, constructive, conservative and continental collision
findings.truth: The lesson's own heading teaches three boundary types and treats continental collision as a form of convergence. The key fact and its revision tip contradicted the body.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the section 'Three Types of Plate Boundary'

findings.claim: The Eduqas examiner reports flag two common errors
findings.truth: House rule: the board is never named in student prose, and no examiner report is being quoted. The two errors themselves are sound teaching points.
findings.evidence: house rule (Eduqas/WJEC neutral phrasing); no source for the examiner-report claim

findings.claim: the Thurston tube on Hawaii (spelled Thúrston)
findings.truth: The feature is the Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. The accent is invented.

findings.claim: damage to the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant cost an estimated US$235 billion
findings.truth: US$235 billion is the World Bank estimate for the whole 2011 earthquake and tsunami disaster, the costliest natural disaster on record, not the cost of the nuclear plant alone.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, 2011 Tohoku earthquake and tsunami (whole-disaster damage estimate; no US$235bn plant figure)

findings.claim: Grindavik evacuated before the November and December 2023 eruptions
findings.truth: No eruption occurred in November 2023. Grindavik was evacuated on 10 November 2023 after a 15 km magma intrusion; the first eruption was on 18 December 2023 near Hagafell.

findings.claim: vertical-evacuation buildings are constructed inland of risk zones
findings.truth: Vertical-evacuation structures are built inside the inundation zone precisely because there is no time to move inland; people climb rather than travel.

findings.claim: The same magnitude earthquake can kill 230,000 in Haiti and 18,500 in Japan
findings.truth: Haiti 2010 was M7.0 and Tohoku 2011 was M9.0. The lesson body states this; the takeaway contradicted it.

findings.claim: examiners want a named hazard pair
findings.truth: No examiner statement supports this. The advice itself is sound; the attribution is invented.

findings.claim: Pinatubo 1991 evacuated 60,000 people two months in advance
findings.truth: Monitoring by PHIVOLCS and USGS ran for about two months; the evacuations happened in the days before the 15 June eruption.
findings.evidence: lesson body (which states it correctly); Pinatubo eruption timeline

findings.claim: a storm surge that pushed sea levels up to 5.6 m above normal in places, killing 326 people in eastern England
findings.truth: 307 people died in Lincolnshire, Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex; 326 is the UK land total (307 England plus 19 Scotland). The 5.6 m figure is water level above mean sea level, not the surge above normal.

findings.claim: The 2020 Cyclone Amphan, despite being more powerful, killed around 100 people in Bangladesh
findings.truth: Amphan killed 26 people in Bangladesh and 103 in India, 133 in total.

findings.claim: At Mappleton, sea defences (rock groynes and an offshore reef) built in 1991
findings.truth: Mappleton was defended in 1991 with two large rock groynes and rock revetments at a cost of about 2 million pounds. There is no offshore reef.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Mappleton, East Riding of Yorkshire

findings.claim: over 30 villages have been lost since Roman times (Holderness)
findings.truth: Published counts give at least 23 lost towns and villages; the commonly taught figure is 29. No source supports more than 30.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Holderness ('at least 23 towns and villages')

findings.claim: Bangladesh has built around 12,000 km of embankments and over 14,000 cyclone shelters since the 1991 cyclone
findings.truth: The coastal embankment network was built from the 1960s Coastal Embankment Project onwards. Only the shelter programme expanded after 1991.

findings.claim: Eduqas examiners reward specific place detail and clear comparison
findings.truth: House rule: the board is never named in student prose, and the examiner claim is invented. The advice itself stands.
findings.evidence: house rule (Eduqas/WJEC neutral phrasing); no source

findings.claim: Shoreline Management Plans divide England's coastline into about 22 sediment cells
findings.truth: 22 was the number of plans covering England and Wales; there are 20 SMPs for the English coast today. Sediment cells are a separate, much smaller set of large littoral cells.
findings.evidence: gov.uk, Shoreline management plans (SMPs): 'There are 20 SMPs covering the English coast'

findings.claim: 8-mark evaluate question labelled '[8 marks]', and the mark scheme opens 'Use the StudyVault rubric.'
findings.truth: Extended-writing questions on this paper carry 4 SPaG marks, so the label should read 8 marks plus 4 SPaG as in the other three lessons. The rubric line is a build instruction left in a student-facing field.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section (SPaG assessed in specified extended-writing questions); sibling lessons

findings.claim: The unit teaches Tectonic Landscapes and Hazards (L1-L2) and Coastal Hazards and their Management (L3-L4) side by side, with no lesson saying a student answers only one of them.
findings.truth: In the option section of this paper a student answers ONE structured question from a choice of two, so only one of these two themes is needed. Options: (a) add one neutral sentence to the lesson 1 and lesson 3 exam tips saying you answer one option question, not both; (b) leave it, on the grounds that the unit is a two-option resource and the choice is a teacher decision. Recommendation: (a) - one sentence in each exam tip, no board named.
findings.evidence: spec summary of assessment: 'One structured question (from a choice of two) assessing either Theme 3 or Theme 4'
findings.ruling: One neutral sentence added to the L1 and L3 exam tips.

findings.claim: The Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain stretches over 5,800 km
findings.truth: True as a lower bound, but the usual published length is about 6,200 km. Not wrong, so not edited.

findings.claim: The 2010 Haiti earthquake killed an estimated 230,000 people
findings.truth: Estimates range from about 100,000 to 316,000. 230,000 is the common teaching figure and the lesson says 'estimated', so it is left alone.

findings.claim: Japanese schools run earthquake drills monthly
findings.truth: Drills are legally required and frequent, but the standard pattern is several times a year rather than monthly. No settled national figure found, so no edit.

findings.claim: Around 30% of the Netherlands sits below sea level
findings.truth: The usual figure is about 26% of the land area (about a third if land at risk of flooding is included). Close enough not to mislead.

findings.claim: the Maldives ... limited income (US$13,000 GNI per capita)
findings.truth: World Bank GNI per capita is about US$12,000 and the Maldives is an upper-middle-income country, the richest in South Asia per head. The figure is roughly right but 'limited income' oversimplifies.

findings.claim: around 800,000 people protected by improved Environment Agency forecasts during the 2013 and 2014 winter storms
findings.truth: Environment Agency reporting for that winter counts properties protected by flood defences, not people protected by forecasts. No matching published figure found, so no edit.

findings.claim: 348 properties in the village of Selsey area
findings.truth: Selsey is a town, not a village, and the phrase is garbled. Wording only, so no edit.

summary: All four lessons carried fixable errors: two invented examiner claims that also named the board, a false Mauna Loa size comparison, a wrong Paricutin growth figure, US$235bn misattributed to the Fukushima plant, a non-existent November 2023 Icelandic eruption, wrong 1953 flood and Cyclone Amphan death tolls, an invented Mappleton offshore reef, an overstated Holderness village count, and sediment cells confused with the number of Shoreline Management Plans. Answer keys were sound apart from the figures they inherited; every knowledge-check key was recomputed and correct.
